statement: The County of Anjou — the Plantagenet dynasty's ancestral domain — was held by the Plantagenet kings of England as part of the Angevin Empire until its conquest by Philip II Augustus of France (1204). Geoffrey V of Anjou's marriage to Empress Matilda of England (daughter of Henry I) created the Plantagenet dynasty when their son became Henry II. Anjou provided the dynasty's military culture and administrative traditions; the term 'Angevin' (from Anjou) describes both the French comital and the English royal family. The loss of Anjou in 1204 severed the dynastic-territorial connection that defined the Plantagenet identity.
